name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; tankers hit 5 Nov
summary: More tankers hit in Hormuz on 5 Nov as Iran keeps pressure on after the US vote
state: Tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on 5 Nov as Iran kept up pressure after the US midterms, a day after IRGC claims of mine strikes south of the strait (US News; CBS News). Iran ties reopening the strait to an end to the US naval blockade. Traffic remains materially impeded, meeting the Alert line.
for_you: Shipping delays and higher insurance costs feed into fuel and goods prices; follow FCDO travel advice for the Gulf region.

sources.title: US News — Tankers hit in Hormuz as Iran keeps up pressure after US vote
CBS News — Iran war updates: more ships attacked in Persian Gulf

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
